# Plan for ISSUE-394

Bound aggregate managed-cache growth through coordinator-owned, throttled maintenance and actionable storage warnings. Build on completed #393 (PRs #405, #406, #407); preserve its explicit cleanup authority and safety checks. This phase writes planning artifacts only.

## Dimensions and feasibility

Approved dimensions: multi_area / known / sensitive; approved execution profile: sensitive. Estimated implementation, adversarial review and validation: 10–14 hours within the 16-hour total claim budget. Keep automatic task/worktree retirement unimplemented (off); explicit cleanup already provides it. No background service, OCI garbage collection, remote archival, protected harness edits or unrelated CLI repair.

## What we know

- `internal/storage/inventory.go:143` implements bounded Scan; Resources carry LastUse and accounting completeness (`:85`), and scanner add reads durable use observations. `internal/storage/discovery.go:200` discovers agent/validator build and dependency caches plus legacy Go caches.
- `internal/storage/accounting.go:11` creates a per-resource accounting allowance and `:23` walks contents. Repeating Scan or reclamation for warnings can therefore traverse large trees even when no deletion occurs.
- `internal/storageuse/storage.go` contains AcquireUse, Finish, Observe and AcquireMaintenance: durable pending tokens protect use; complete coverage is required for maintenance; LastUse updates on admission and completion. Existing tests include TestLegacyAndLostRecordsRemainUnknown and TestConcurrentUseAndExclusiveMaintenance (`internal/storageuse/storage_test.go:88,37`). Legacy caches cannot become eligible merely by aging.
- `internal/storage/retention.go:455` is guarded reclamation; `:789` acquires maintenance exclusion, and the removal path validates resource/repository identity and uses root-bound removal. BackendRetention (`:962`) rejects missing or incoherent task/PR evidence. Preserve these checks.
- `internal/cli/storage.go` registers actual cleanup flags apply, all-repos and json. `docs/project.md:287` and `README.md:284` already describe them. Guidance must use `swarm storage cleanup`, `swarm storage cleanup --apply`, and aggregate variants with `--all-repos`; `--json` is supported.
- Operator profile is separate from candidate policy: `internal/contract/types.go:219` NodeProfile; `internal/node/profile.go:58` loads the node file. Existing dependency settings establish the operator-only pattern.
- Node pool executes work at `internal/cli/node.go:177`; issue work entry is `internal/cli/work.go:67`; interactive stage/validate entries are `internal/cli/stage.go:22`, `internal/cli/validate.go:15,97`; PR actions enter `internal/cli/pr.go:49`. Storage lifetime scopes already exist in workflow and validation; maintenance must run after their teardown.
- Operator-supplied scale: 45 GB caches, leaves up to 54,262 entries, 7,000+ control files, 930 resources. Design for this scale without allocating equivalent bytes in tests.
- Makefile check runs format diagnostics, vet, staticcheck, race suite and changelog validation. Operator identifies TestIssuePlanReplanCapAndRecovery as a known main failure; preserve it unchanged.

## What we are assuming

The supplied checkout represents the approved planning source. This sandbox exposes no Git metadata (`git rev-parse HEAD` fails), so approved-base object existence cannot be checked here. All proposed new paths below were checked absent in this snapshot; coordinator/developer must verify the same against approved base before implementation and treat any existing path as modified. Parent #378 plan is unavailable here; this contract and operator instructions define scope, with no dependency on retrieving it.

## Open questions

1. Confirm enclosing storage scopes finish before each selected lifecycle hook; implementation step 3 answers this by tracing defers and testing order, moving hooks outward if needed.
2. Determine bounded pass limits and latency at supplied scale using step 2 fixtures/benchmarks. Incomplete accounting must stay explicit, never imply target achieved. Real-host timing/reclamation and Linux/macOS boundary checks unavailable in the sandbox belong in the PR checklist, not an implementation gate.
3. Full make check may remain red solely for the named pre-existing test. Record exact output and baseline evidence; do not change the test, waive a gate or claim a passing check.

## Design and implementation sequence

### 1. Operator-owned settings

Modify NodeProfile in `internal/contract/types.go` with an optional storage block; add `internal/node/storage.go` and tests to load/validate it only from the operator node profile (default `~/.config/swarm/node.yaml`, existing path resolver). Never read these values from .swarm/config.yaml, a worktree or candidate environment. Proposed fields to implement and then document: cache_target_bytes=42949672960 (40 GiB), inactive_retention=336h (14 days), low_free_bytes=5368709120 (5 GiB), low_free_percent=10, maintenance_interval=30m, warning_interval=10m. Use pointer/optional fields so omission and invalid zero are distinct. Require positive bytes/durations, percent >0 and <=100, checked duration/byte arithmetic; reject negative, overflow, malformed and unknown storage keys. No task-retirement setting in this change. Invalid operator storage settings disable automatic mutation with an advisory diagnostic; explicit configuration inspection reports the error. Preserve workflow results.

### 2. Shared maintenance engine

Add `internal/storage/maintenance.go` and `maintenance_test.go`; modify `retention.go`, `inventory.go`, `discovery.go`, `accounting.go` and existing tests only where needed to share bounded enumeration/accounting and guarded deletion. Do not implement maintenance by calling Scan followed by ApplyReclamation: that repeats discovery and usage walks. Introduce an internal pass inventory reusable for aggregate accounting, selection, warnings and reclamation. Explicit #393 cleanup keeps its existing semantics and guards.

- Enter a coordinator-private, safefs-rooted, host-wide cross-process admission lock and durable throttle before registry enumeration, control-record enumeration, cache walking or remote access. Store bounded timestamps/summary separately from granted cache roots. Atomically reserve a pass at start to throttle failures too; use nonblocking lock admission, bounded context (initially 60 seconds), serial eviction and cancellation throughout. Failed admission skips maintenance. Missing/corrupt throttle data may permit one guarded pass, never deletion without evidence; concurrent callers cannot all scan. Handle clock rollback conservatively without permanently suppressing maintenance.
- Maintenance and warning deadlines are independent. At 10-minute warning calls use cheap filesystem free-space observations and cached inventory summary; do not refresh expensive inventory until 30-minute maintenance is due. Mark cached data stale/incomplete. On repeated calls within both intervals perform neither tree walks nor remote calls, including across CLI processes.
- One bounded inventory per pass across registered repositories and selected current checkout, deduplicated by canonical common-directory key. Enumerate each control record once, share accounting once per cache leaf, bound memory/entries/depth and all remote page/record counts. Do not query PRs per cache. Batch repository evidence once per repository where existing guarded retention requires it; retain unknown/offline scopes. Do not fetch/requery to render warnings.
- Cache-only automatic candidates: agent-build, validate-build (Go, Rust, C/C++), agent-deps, validate-deps. Never delete task state, worktrees, branches, scratch, operator-shared caches or unknown legacy caches automatically. Sum unique observed allocated cache bytes across repositories; partial/unsupported allocation accounting is an explicitly incomplete lower bound, not zero.
- Eligible units need complete durable use coverage, no unresolved uses and trustworthy LastUse. Sort by LastUse ascending with deterministic identity tie-break. Retention means minimum idle age: delete aged eligible units oldest first to approach the aggregate target; keep recent inactive units even when over budget. Below target no budget eviction. Filesystem mtime, PID exit and repository inactivity alone never prove eligibility.
- Extend storageuse maintenance guard to expose its locked observation without tokens. Recheck LastUse, eligibility, identity and accounting under admission exclusion immediately before deleting; if a unit was reused after snapshot, skip it this pass. Keep exclusion through deletion and preserve existing root-bound removal, retention and prune safety. Deduct only confirmed namespace removal observations; never promise physical savings with hardlinks/open files. Do not rewalk retained units for after-accounting. If target cannot be reached, report observed excess, unknown/protected amounts and cleanup guidance.

### 3. Lifecycle and diagnostics

Add `internal/cli/storage_maintenance.go` and tests to adapt node settings, registry/scopes, trackers, output and injected clock/filesystem/remote counters. Modify `root.go`, `node.go`, `work.go`, `stage.go`, `validate.go` and `pr.go` to call this adapter only for coordinator-owned execution: before work starts and after the outer execution returns and scopes finish; node pool startup and each completed job; issue/PR work, stage and validate plus repo validate. Gate out worker gateways, fork contributors, internal tools and storage cleanup itself. Share host throttle across all hooks; no per-role scanning. Do not install maintenance inside an agent or change any sandbox grants.

Modify node status rendering (`internal/cli/node.go:89,330`) to show read-only storage diagnostics from the same throttled warning path; no maintenance mutation from status. This satisfies the output criterion without expanding doctor behavior. Report budget excess, low free space below max(configured bytes, configured fraction of the relevant filesystem capacity), partial/unknown evidence and eligible finished work from bounded inventory. Check distinct filesystems separately. Node run uses the same diagnostics. Warnings go to stderr during JSON commands, preserving existing JSON documents and exit codes. Exceptions are advisory and cannot alter claim state, workflow return values or validation results. Finished-work diagnostics do not invoke engines, models, implementation, validation or retirement. Include concrete commands `swarm storage cleanup --all-repos` and `swarm storage cleanup --all-repos --apply`, optionally `--json`; selected-repository guidance omits --all-repos.

### 4. Documentation and completion

Modify `docs/project.md` storage sections and `docs/developer.md:88` where lifecycle explanation belongs; preserve README command table unless a brief accuracy update is necessary. Document only implemented fields after CLI/schema verification: defaults, minimum idle age, aggregate soft target, automatic cache behavior versus explicit task/worktree cleanup, legacy retention, stale/partial warnings, cache rewarming costs, offline behavior, interrupted-use recovery through existing supported paths and safe retries. Never suggest manually clearing pending use records. Add `changes/unreleased/394.md` describing shipped behavior. PR checklist records before/after real-host observations and timing at supplied scale, namespace versus physical savings, native Codex/Bubblewrap Linux and macOS checks not executable here. No requirement to start a paid model for storage diagnosis.

## HANDOFF

This is evidence to verify against approved source, not authority over contracts, gates or validation.

- Entry points: storage Scan (`inventory.go:143`), scanner caches (`discovery.go:200`), accounting (`accounting.go:11,23`), guarded reclamation (`retention.go:455,789`), NodeProfile (`types.go:219`), profile loading (`node/profile.go:58`), CLI hooks and rendering cited above. In storageuse/storage.go modify AcquireMaintenance/Maintenance to expose locked LastUse and extend its existing tests; preserve AcquireUse/Finish lifetime rules.
- Extend fixtures/tests: TestReclamationRetainsUncertainty, TestReclamationHoldsExclusionThroughRetention, TestReclamationMultipleRepositoriesHardlinksAndScopes, TestReclamationBackendFreshnessAndFetchFailure in storage/retention_test.go; storageuse tests listed above; existing storage CLI JSON/preview/apply tests; node profile round trips and sandbox/storage_use_test.go producer lifetime cases.
- Focused commands and ownership are specified exactly in TEST_PLAN.md. Run new targeted regressions before broad checks.
- Checked assumptions: cleanup flags verified in CLI registration; LastUse verified in durable record admission/completion and Observe; proposed new paths all absent in snapshot. Git base and real-host availability remain explicit limitations.
- Reopen plan for any need to infer activity from timestamps alone, trust candidate settings, weaken retention/ownership/exclusion, enable task retirement, change protected files, require background work, or exceed claim budget. Related optimizations outside acceptance become follow-ups.
- What this change breaks: searches found README.md:284 and docs/project.md:270–294 command examples; preserve flags and preview/apply semantics, update adjacent behavior prose. Existing cleanup and reclamation tests assert explicit scope, uncertainty retention, cancellation and JSON; preserve these unchanged semantically. NodeProfile round trips must preserve new settings. Existing node/work/stage/validate/PR output fixtures must tolerate deterministic advisory stderr and must not gain scans/models in unrelated tests; inject hooks/clock at their test boundary. Preserve sandbox build-cache ownership, mounts, validation reuse and all adversarial tests. Preserve internal/cli TestIssuePlanReplanCapAndRecovery unchanged.
- New files: internal/storage/maintenance.go, maintenance_test.go; internal/node/storage.go, storage_test.go; internal/cli/storage_maintenance.go, storage_maintenance_test.go; changes/unreleased/394.md. All absent in supplied snapshot; approved-base absence requires coordinator verification because Git metadata is not exposed.

# Test plan for ISSUE-394

Planning artifact; checks below are to be executed against implementation, not claims of passing results. Sensitive work requires independent adversarial review. Tests use temporary trusted operator roots, injected clock/usage/remote adapters and local/GitHub tracker fixtures; no live model or destructive real-host cleanup.

## Acceptance coverage

| AC | Concrete verification |
| --- | --- |
| 1: validated operator settings | New TestStorageSettingsDefaultsAndValidation in internal/node/storage_test.go: all defaults, omitted/zero distinction, negative/overflow bytes and durations, malformed percent/duration, unknown storage keys, round trips. TestStorageCandidateConfigIgnored supplies hostile candidate .swarm/config.yaml, worktree and environment values and proves effective settings come only from node profile. Missing profile defaults; unreadable/malformed profile disables mutation and gives advisory output without affecting work. |
| 2: aggregate oldest-inactive eviction | New TestMaintenanceAggregateBudgetAndOrder in internal/storage/maintenance_test.go: many repositories individually under any old Go limit but collectively above 40 GiB; synthetic byte observations avoid large files. Matrix Go, Rust, C/C++, agent/validator build/dependency leaves; oldest LastUse first, deterministic ties, minimum 14-day age, stop near target, below-target no deletion. Deliberately reverse filesystem mtime order to prove use-record ordering. Local and GitHub bounded evidence variants, no per-entry remote calls. |
| 3: protected use/excess | TestMaintenanceProtectsConsumers: channel-controlled prefetch/read/write/validation admissions, including overlapping uses and unverified stop. Attempt eviction while each consumer is live; preserve data and report excess plus exact commands. Reuse a unit between snapshot and lock and verify locked LastUse causes skip. Producer integrations extend sandbox/storage_use_test.go and validation dependency/build-cache fixtures rather than merely mocking activity. Legacy/no-record, corrupt/missing record, unresolved old use and unknown ownership always retain. |
| 4: actionable output | New TestStorageMaintenanceDiagnostics in internal/cli/storage_maintenance_test.go: node status and node run show over-target, low-space and eligible finished work; commands are swarm storage cleanup and swarm storage cleanup --apply, with --all-repos for aggregate scope and optional --json. Inject model/engine/validation spies that fail on invocation during status; prove none run. Preserve stdout JSON and return code; warnings on stderr. |
| 5: failure safety | TestMaintenanceFailureIsolation and CLI lifecycle fixtures inject offline GitHub, failed PR pages, unknown status, incomplete registration/accounting, permissions, timeout, partial removal, corrupt throttle, failed durable write and cancellation. Unknown task status never becomes merged/eligible. Snapshot serialized claims and workflow outputs before/after failures; assert identical result/error/claim state, no claim CAS writes, no task/worktree retirement. Test low-space byte/percentage max, equal threshold, separate filesystems and unavailable free-space observation. Protected-over-budget reports honest residual excess; partial totals remain unknown/lower bounds. |
| 6: zero work while throttled | TestMaintenanceThrottleCounters uses injected directory-open/entry/recursive-accounting/control-enumeration/remote counters at actual expensive boundaries, not just a mocked high-level Scan. Repeated startup/after-run calls under 10m keep all counters unchanged; at 10m cheap free-space/cached-warning refresh only, no walk/remote; at 30m exactly one inventory pass. Independent service instances sharing durable state simulate successive CLI processes; concurrent processes and node workers admit at most one pass. Failure attempts are throttled; cancellation and clock rollback are covered. |
| 7: task retirement off | TestMaintenanceNeverRetiresTasks runs default and customized operator settings against finished and unfinished tasks and asserts worktrees/branches/state unchanged. No automatic-retirement opt-in is introduced. Existing explicit storage cleanup preview/apply tests continue covering the sole retirement path from #393. |
| 8: operator docs/checklist | Review docs/project.md and docs/developer.md against implemented storage fields and CLI registrations. Verify defaults and automatic versus explicit behavior, rewarming, recovery and legacy retention. PR checklist includes real-host reclamation/timing, Linux native Codex/Bubblewrap and macOS unavailable checks, with observed or not-run status and reason. These are review evidence, not a sandbox implementation blocker. |
| 9: shipped scope/changelog/checks | Review changes/unreleased/394.md and documentation for implemented-only claims; run focused checks below and make check once at final candidate. Preserve the known main TestIssuePlanReplanCapAndRecovery failure and record it if encountered; never represent a failing make check as passing. |

## Developer-owned focused checks

Implement meaningful tests under the proposed TestStorageSettings/TestStorageCandidate/TestMaintenance/TestStorageMaintenance prefixes. Use exact commands:

```bash
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/node -run '^Test(StorageSettings|StorageCandidate)' -count=1
go test -race -timeout=10m ./internal/storage ./internal/storageuse -count=1
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/cli -run '^Test(Storage|Maintenance)' -count=1
```

Check changed Go files with `gofmt -s -l` (list concrete changed files), format only changes. Ensure new tests match the specified regexes; rename/add command selectors if necessary and record actual commands. Add targeted lifecycle tests to the CLI selector when their names fall outside it. Run affected existing node profile tests as well as new settings tests. Existing storage/report/cleanup regressions must remain meaningful.

Scale fixture: represent at least 930 resources and 7,000 control entries via bounded lazy adapters, and one on-disk or lazy deep leaf of 54,262 entries. Synthetic aggregate allocated bytes exceed 45 GB; no need to allocate those bytes. Count enumeration/accounting operations and peak retained budget, assert one inventory per due pass, no rewalk of retained resources, bounded cancellation and no per-leaf remote queries. Include duplicate scopes, hardlinks, unsafe symlinks, special files, path swaps and resource reuse after snapshot. Time benchmarks are advisory; correctness uses counters rather than fragile wall-clock thresholds. If limits are exhausted retain uncertain resources and show incomplete diagnostics.

CLI help verification after implementation:

```bash

go run ./cmd/swarm node status --help

```

Validate changed doc links/anchors against files and new shell examples with `bash -n` using extracted snippets. Cross-check every documented field against the implemented operator settings loader, not candidate schema. Do not run real cleanup --apply as a documentation test.

## Tester-owned independent review and result reuse

Independently read WorkUnit AC1–9 and changed source; verify operator provenance, all cache classes/owners, post-consumer hook ordering, lock lifetime and locked last-use selection, root-bound deletion, throttle placement, bounded accounting, fresh guarded retention and failure isolation. Inspect actual injected counter locations to ensure a throttled call cannot walk a tree before the measured hook. Review default-off task retirement and confirm no candidate-supplied cleanup tools or credential/mount changes.

Reuse applicable passing developer command outputs bound to the same source, including race results. Repeat commands only for relevant source changes, observed failures or unresolved coverage concerns. Add focused adversarial checks if evidence misses a case; do not rerun the complete suite solely for role transition. Record evidence per AC, remaining platform gaps and unresolved findings.

## Coordinator-owned final reference policy

The coordinator runs the complete trusted-base required policy once after roles finish; it is not a per-role checklist. Agent results are advisory and do not satisfy claim-bound validation/publication. AC9 additionally requires one final `make check`; reuse its complete applicable results rather than duplicate full race runs without cause. The coordinator records any policy gaps separately.

Known baseline: internal/cli TestIssuePlanReplanCapAndRecovery fails on main per operator. Do not edit, skip or weaken it or alter Makefile to make checks green. If make check fails there, record precise failure and any other failures, use focused passing coverage to distinguish this change, and leave gate disposition to the coordinator/maintainer. No claim of passing make check until it actually passes.

PR review checklist records host cache size/resource count before and after an explicitly operator-approved real-host run, preview/apply commands, observed reclaimed namespace/allocated bytes, elapsed pass and throttled-call costs, cache rewarming, and unavailable OS/runtime checks. Linux/macOS native Codex and harness-tools Bubblewrap coverage uses fixtures here; actual unavailable platform checks remain clearly labeled. Human plan approval is required before implementation; no agent verdict substitutes for that gate.

# Implementation Summary (Issue #394)

## What we learned

- Test control-root resolvers must follow per-fixture cache overrides; a fixed suite root mixes durable pending-use evidence between tests and hides ownership-boundary checks.
- Give serial usage accounting a separate pass budget from discovery and durable-use evidence, so one deep cache cannot exhaust later resources' eligibility observations.

## Working Tree Changes
```text
 M internal/cli/storage_maintenance.go
 M internal/cli/storage_maintenance_test.go
 M internal/storage/maintenance.go
?? changes/unreleased/394-status.md
```

## Developer report

# ISSUE-394 focused status correction

Implemented only the operator-requested correction to the existing approved implementation.

Read-only maintenance now reads the bounded cached throttle summary and returns it on every status request, regardless of warning admission. It neither acquires/creates the lifecycle admission lock nor creates the maintenance directory or writes throttle state. Cached inventory gets a fresh stale flag in memory. Existing cheap free-space observations still run only when the warning deadline is due. Lifecycle maintenance and warning admission are unchanged.

Status always renders an existing inventory, including healthy inventories, with its age. Observed/excess bytes include decimal GB alongside exact bytes. When InventoryAt is absent, status explicitly says no storage inventory exists yet and lists the lifecycle hooks that will produce one. No tree walk or remote request is introduced.

## Verification

All results apply to the final source. Focused checks only; the broader implementation's prior evidence is recorded in WORKUNIT/REVIEW. No broad CLI campaign, make check, host cleanup or publication was performed for this small correction. The operator-designated baseline TestIssuePlanReplanCapAndRecovery remains unchanged.

- `go test -timeout=2m ./internal/cli -run '^TestStorageMaintenance' -count=1`: PASS, package 0.007s.
- `go test -race -timeout=2m ./internal/storage -run '^TestMaintenance(ThrottleCounters|ConcurrentAdmissionAndFailure)$' -count=1`: PASS, package 1.044s.
- `go vet ./internal/cli ./internal/storage`: PASS, tool elapsed 0.767s.
- `go tool staticcheck ./internal/cli ./internal/storage`: PASS, completed in approximately 3s across asynchronous tool calls.
- `gofmt -s -l internal/cli/storage_maintenance.go internal/cli/storage_maintenance_test.go internal/storage/maintenance.go`: PASS, no output.
- `go run ./cmd/changelog --check`: PASS. Combined formatting/changelog tool elapsed 0.058s.

New CLI regression uses the same adapter function as production and real Maintain with temporary throttle state. Repeated calls assert both summaries (60.7 GB observed, 17.8 GB excess), age, stderr-only output, unchanged throttle bytes, and zero injected directory/Git/retention counters. Missing inventory is checked twice and never creates throttle state. Tests require no repository or model invocation.

## HANDOFF

Changed files:
- internal/storage/maintenance.go: read-only cached-summary branch before lifecycle lock/throttle writes.
- internal/cli/storage_maintenance.go: shared injectable-options adapter; unconditional status summary, age and no-inventory message; human units.
- internal/cli/storage_maintenance_test.go: fast repeated-status and never-run regressions with actual boundary counters.
- changes/unreleased/394-status.md: focused operator-visible fix.

Commands and results are listed above for tester reuse. No additional acceptance criterion or environment-dependent host behavior was claimed verified. Existing real-host/platform review gaps and coordinator-owned full validation remain as recorded in prior artifacts.

<!-- swarm:guidance:start -->
## Operator guidance

> Small fix found by the coordinator on the real host; change only this. swarm node status renders storage diagnostics only when the warning throttle is due, so a second status within 10 minutes prints nothing about storage although the real summary held 60.7 GB observed and 17.8 GB excess. An operator explicitly asking for status must always see it. In read-only status mode, always render the cached summary from throttle.json with its age, doing no tree walk, remote call or throttle write beyond what already exists. Keep the throttle as is for lifecycle warnings on work, stage, validate and node run. When no pass has ever run, say that no storage inventory exists yet and when one will run, rather than 'observed cache bytes=0'. Report bytes in human units such as 17.8 GB alongside exact values if that fits the existing style. Add CLI tests: repeat status shows the summary both times with zero walk and remote counters from the injected counters; never-run state prints the explicit message. Keep internal/cli tests fast. internal/cli TestIssuePlanReplanCapAndRecovery is a known failure on main; leave it alone; a sandbox-only CLI package timeout is environmental.

<!-- swarm:guidance:end -->
